text:
Sam: quick heads-up — support flagged 3 tenants this week that hit hard 429s during short scheduled spikes. We should run an internal ratebench to pick sane RPM/TPM + burst token defaults.

Ryan: can you paste repro steps and current defaults? any auth/billing overlap?

Sam: repro (minimal): curl + repeated requests to /v1/generate with API key under a single client id. Current defaults we ship for self-serve: 60 RPM, 600 TPM, burst_tokens=180 (token-bucket). Tenants saw p95 jump and then 429s after ~90s of sustained bursts. No billing issue reported, auth fine.

Sam: example quick repro:
```bash
# single-worker burst (simulate client spamming short convo requests)
for i in {1..120}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","input":"test"}' &
done
wait
```

Maria: +1 for a structured plan. propose we run three profiles in lab:
- sustained: ramp 0 -> target RPS over 5m, hold 10m (to measure steady-state TPM/RPM amplification)
- burst-window: short 30s bursts at 3x target each minute for 10m (to stress burst tokens)
- multi-key: same as sustained but spread across 50 API keys to emulate many users.

Maria: metrics to capture: 200/429/503 counts, p50/p95/p99 latencies, queue length on serving nodes, KV cache hit ratio, token-bucket usage, GPU util, response size. Also capture header-level retry-after and any 5xx stanzas.

Jon: important: separate per-route (generate/embeddings/re-rank) limits. Embeddings have higher token churn and compress differently; they should have their own RPM/TPM profile. Also track per-key vs global enforcement.

Ryan: question on burst semantics — do we keep token-bucket with refill rate = RPM/60 and bucket_size = burst_tokens, or switch to a sliding-window quota? My vote: keep token-bucket but tune size. Sliding windows are noisy with many clients.

Sam: agree on token-bucket. For example, if we want to allow 120 RPM steady with a 30s burst window:
- refill_rate = 120/60 = 2 tokens/sec
- to allow 30s full-burst, bucket_size ~= 2 * 30 = 60 tokens (plus fudge for concurrent requests -> multiply by avg concurrency)
So buckets are small for low-RPM clients; multi-key tests will show aggregate behavior.

Maria: sample k6 snippet for sustained run:
```js
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';
export let options = { vus: 200, duration: '15m', rps: 50 };
export default function () {
  http.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', JSON.stringify({model:'rwd-7b', input:'load test'}), {headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer '+__ENV.API_KEY}});
  sleep(0.1);
}
```

Jon: make sure we run with realistic seq lengths for tokens. Embedding calls are shorter but CPU-bound; generation calls vary. If you only test tiny inputs you will under-provision. Add a 1–2% long-tail test with 2k token responses.

Sam: noted. Also capture behavior when a key exhausts quota: do we return 429 with a Retry-After header (preferred), and log the exhausted_quota metric for SRE alerts. Support wants clearer error bodies for customers.

Ryan: small nit — add a test where the control plane denies a rebuilt key (auth failure) concurrent with load to ensure no weird 401/429 mix. We saw one case where clients got 401 then a shower of 429s when retries resumed.

DevOps Bot: scheduled run created: https://internal-loadlab.redwood/jobs/1976543210 (ETA: tomorrow 03:30 UTC). Config: sustained 100 RPS target, burst-profile 300 RPS for 30s per min, multi-key fanout 100 keys.

Maria: nice. For analysis, produce a CSV per run with columns: timestamp, route, key_id_hash, status_code, latency_ms, tokens_consumed, bucket_level, node_id. That lets us pivot.

Sam: on thresholds — proposal for defaults after we iterate: self-serve baseline -> RPM 120, TPM 1,200, burst_tokens 240. For enterprise/dedicated we can raise per-contract. These numbers are placeholders until lab results.

Jon: also add policy for graceful degradation: when node-level queue > 500ms or GPU util > 85% we start shed non-critical routes (e.g., rerank) and respond with 429 + Retry-After for generate. Document fallback logic in console.

Ryan: logging snippet we saw in customer's tenant:
```
2026-02-27T14:21:03Z ERROR quota_enforcer: denied request key=abc123 route=/v1/generate reason=token_bucket_empty remaining=0
2026-02-27T14:21:03Z INFO http: respond 429 Retry-After=12
```

Sam: perfect. Action items: @Maria build k6 job templates + csv exporter, @Ryan add test harness to rotate API keys and record bucket_level metrics, @Jon update per-route limit map and write a short doc for support on error body interpretation. I'll summarize results and propose final default numbers in a follow-up PR.

Maria: on it. I'll include dashboards (SLO burn, per-route error heatmap).

Ryan: I'll add heap of instrumentation to the lab build — token rates, leak rate, short window counters.

DevOps Bot: job started by Maria on host loadlab-23 at 1976543270

Sam: thanks everyone — feel free to drop quick notes here if you see surprises during the run. :thumbsup:
